A griefer sends 1 wei of sUSDS to the pair and calls sync(). exitAndSeed then reverts with PairNotEmpty(1,0,1,0). abort() returns the whole BPT to the old pooler, and the old pooler is left usable, because BalancerPoolerV2 keeps no BPT accounting (withdrawBPT and rescueERC20 are plain transfers). The pair is therefore public across several broadcast txs (createPair, UniPoolerV2 deploy, escrow deploy, withdrawBPT, owner BPT transfer, exitAndSeed).

LOCAL-002.description: Only four tokens can ever leave the escrow (_bpt, _sUSDS, _phUSD, _usds). Any other ERC20 sent to it is permanently locked (no rescue, no owner). The BPT address is SNAPSHOTTED from oldPooler.pool(), which is owner-mutable via BalancerPoolerV2.setPool, while BalancerPoolerV2.withdrawBPT transfers IERC20(_pool) — the CURRENT pool. If oldPooler.setPool is called between escrow deployment and withdrawBPT(escrow, amt) (or the owner hand-transfers a BPT of a different pool), the BPT that lands on the escrow is not _bpt: exitAndSeed reverts NoBPT and abort does not return it, so it is permanently stranded. Likewise any mis-sent token (e.g. USDC, a wrong BPT, an LP token) is unrecoverable. Story open question #5 accepts 'no rescue for tokens outside the four (INFO)'; the setPool interaction is the non-obvious part.
LOCAL-002.recommendation: Operational: assert escrow.bpt() == oldPooler.pool() immediately before withdrawBPT in the cutover core (story-103), and never call setPool during the cutover window. Optionally allow abort() to return an arbitrary non-protected token to oldPooler (destination still fixed, so custody guarantee is preserved).

PATTERN-MR-002.description: _bpt is snapshotted from oldPooler.pool(), but BalancerPoolerV2.setPool is owner-mutable and withdrawBPT pays IERC20(_pool) (the CURRENT pool). If setPool runs between escrow deploy and withdrawBPT, and oldPooler holds the new pool's BPT, then the escrow receives a token it can neither exit (NoBPT) nor abort. The escrow has no generic rescue, so that token is stranded forever. Would a competent owner be surprised by this? Plausibly yes (Law 3 footgun), though the precondition is unlikely.

The escrow receives token X, not its snapshot _bpt. exitAndSeed reverts NoBPT, and abort() moves only _bpt/_sUSDS/_phUSD/_usds (L296-299), so X stays stranded in the escrow forever. The escrow has no owner, no rescue path and immutable addresses. Refinement: the original BPT is not lost, because it stays on the old pooler and the owner can rescue it with rescueERC20. PATTERN-003.description: The seed ratio is s:p = the escrow's whole sUSDS and phUSD balances after a proportional or recovery exit. CODE-003.relation: refines LOCAL-003 / PATTERN-002 (weak minAmountsOut). Cross-contract seed-price manipulation CLEARED. Informational.
CODE-003.description: The seed ratio is whatever composition the Balancer pool has at exit, and story-103's floors are quoted from live state. So a pre-skewed Balancer pool would be baked into both the floors and the V2 seed price. Checked against mainnet: the pool is a 50/50 weighted pool, which is constant-product like V2, with no hooks and a 0.3% fee. For two constant-product venues an LP position's value at a given price depends only on its invariant. If an attacker skews the Balancer price and the escrow exits and seeds at the skewed price, arbitraging both venues back returns the attacker roughly their own slippage, minus 0.3% fees on each leg. POL is not extracted. Hookless pool: no V3 hook can adjust amounts or call back. Residual risk is limited to wrong-order or loose floors (PATTERN-002). The escrow cannot check order, so the core should assert getPoolTokenInfo order [sUSDS, phUSD] when building minAmountsOut.

ECON-001.relation: Quantitatively CONFIRMS CODE-003 / LOCAL-003 (cleared). Not a new finding.
ECON-001.description:
Setup: a public-mempool sandwich around exitAndSeed on the real fork. The attacker pre-skews the Balancer pool to just inside the exit floors, the escrow exits and seeds at the skewed ratio, and the attacker then arbitrages BOTH the new V2 pair and the 37.1% Balancer remainder back to the pre-attack price. Both venues are 50/50 constant-product with a 0.3% fee. The protocol's seeded invariant is therefore preserved, and the back-arb returns exactly the attacker's own slippage, minus fees on both legs.

Fork numbers (p0 = 0.830781 sUSDS/phUSD):
- tol 1%: seed price moved to 0.8473 (buy direction) or 0.8146 (sell direction), i.e. +/-2.0%. Attacker PnL is -1.753 sUSDS in both directions. The protocol's V2 position is worth 37,313.63 sUSDS at p0 against a 37,312.67 baseline (+0.96), and sqrtK rises from 20,468.354 to 20,468.882.
- tol 5%: seed price moved to 0.9187 or 0.7513 (+10.6% / -9.6%). Attacker PnL is -8.808 sUSDS. The protocol gains +4.82 sUSDS at p0, and sqrtK rises to 20,470.996.

Organic off-peg case, where the pre-cutover price is not attacker-induced: phUSD is at $0.9238. phUSD is mint-only at $1 through PhusdStableMinter, with no redeem or withdraw (phoenix-protocol-explained.md: 'deliberately not redeemable'). So no below-peg arbitrage exists. The only other venue is the Balancer remainder, which sits at the identical price after the proportional exit. An arbitrageur therefore extracts 0 from the freshly seeded pair. If phUSD were above $1 at cutover, the mint-and-sell arbitrage would take the same skim from POL on Balancer as on V2 (same curve, same fee). The plan states that skim is intended (BalancerWinddownPlan.md L502-506 'Pushing through the mint price is intended'). Neither case is a value leak introduced by the escrow, and the escrow does not change the L-22/L-24/Q-20 bounds.
ECON-001.economicImpact: None to the protocol. The protocol's invariant strictly increases, from the attacker's fees.
ECON-001.attackScenario:
1. Swap X sUSDS->phUSD (or the reverse) on the Balancer pool, up to the floor tolerance.
2. exitAndSeed exits pro rata and seeds V2 at the skewed ratio.
3. Arbitrage V2 and the Balancer remainder back to p0. Net: -fees.
ECON-001.profitability: Never profitable: -1.75 sUSDS at a 1% tolerance, -8.81 sUSDS at 5%.

ECON-002.function: exitAndSeed / _exit (floors computed off-chain by phStaging2 UniPoolerCutoverCore)
ECON-002.description: story-052 justifies the immutable-operator gate partly on the grounds that a stranger 'front-running between the owner's withdrawBPT and exitAndSeed ... would revert the forge broadcast mid-cutover'. story-103 broadcasts through the public mempool (forge --broadcast --slow --ledger --legacy, with no private relay), using 'live proportional share minus a tight tolerance' floors that are quoted at simulation time. The gate does not stop the cheapest version of that front-run: any Balancer swap that moves one side by more than the tolerance makes the Vault revert. Fork-proven at the repo's 1 bp tolerance: a 4 sUSDS->phUSD Balancer swap makes exitAndSeed revert with AmountOutBelowMin(phUSD, 22,453.35e18, 22,454.12e18). The griefer then unwinds for a round-trip cost of 0.024 sUSDS (about $0.027) plus gas. Organic Balancer flow during the multi-tx --slow broadcast can trip the same check. Funds are safe: the tx is atomic, the BPT stays in the escrow, and the operator can re-quote and retry, or abort. But the cutover can be held hostage for pennies per attempt, and per the plan a mid-broadcast revert poisons the progress file. ECON-001 proves that a loose floor gives up no value, because a sandwich is net-negative for the attacker. So the 'tight tolerance' buys no economic protection and only maximises griefability.
ECON-002.economicImpact: No value loss. Availability only: each cutover attempt can be reverted for about $0.03 plus gas, and with --slow the attack window spans several blocks.
ECON-002.attackScenario:
1. Watch the mempool for the escrow deploy, withdrawBPT, or exitAndSeed.
2. Front-run exitAndSeed with a ~4 sUSDS Balancer swap (1 bp tolerance) or a ~tol*Y swap generally.
3. exitAndSeed reverts AmountOutBelowMin; the forge script halts before wiring.
4. Unwind; repeat on retry.
ECON-002.profitability: Not profitable. Griefing cost is about 0.024 sUSDS plus gas per revert at 1 bp. The cost scales as about 0.6*tol*35.7k*0.003 sUSDS, so a 2% tolerance raises it to roughly 1.3 sUSDS of fees plus the slippage the griefer must stomach.
ECON-002.recommendation: phStaging2:103 core: (a) use a moderate exit tolerance (for example 1-3%), since ECON-001 shows wider floors cost POL nothing; and/or (b) submit exitAndSeed through a private relay (Flashbots Protect); and (c) document the 'exitAndSeed reverted: re-quote and resume from receipts' runbook step. No escrow code change is needed.

F-01-052.actualBehavior: The operator gate stops one front-run variant: a stranger calling exitAndSeed first, which would seed the pair and make the owner's later exitAndSeed revert PairNotEmpty. It does not stop the cheaper variant, which needs no call to the escrow at all: a Balancer swap that moves either side of the proportional share by more than the floor tolerance. Econ fork-proved this at the repo's 1 bp tolerance. A 4 sUSDS->phUSD swap makes exitAndSeed revert AmountOutBelowMin(phUSD, 22,453.35e18, 22,454.12e18), at a round-trip cost of about $0.03. story-103 broadcasts through the public mempool (`--broadcast --skip-simulation --slow --ledger --legacy`, 103 L99) as separate transactions, and the floors are quoted before the broadcast. So the gate does not deliver the mid-cutover-revert protection the story credits to it. Organic Balancer flow can trip the same check.
F-01-052.deviation: The code is faithful to the design. The story's rationale for that design is inaccurate: it says the operator gate prevents a front-run that reverts the broadcast mid-cutover, but the dominant way to cause that revert bypasses the gate. Law-1 assessment: the story's intent is not unsafe. The transaction is atomic, the BPT stays in the escrow, and the operator can re-quote and retry or abort() to the old pooler, so no value can be extracted (ECON-001 shows a sandwich within the floors is net-negative for the attacker). The residual is liveness only, so this is not escalated as story-unsafe. Spec correction: the story and the 103 runbook should state that floor-tolerance reverts are expected and recoverable, and that the tolerance should be sized for griefing resistance rather than 'tight'. ECON-001 shows a loose floor gives up no value on two constant-product venues. The runbook should also say whether the escrow deploy, withdrawBPT and exitAndSeed run in one broadcast, and how the progress file resumes after an exitAndSeed revert.

(e.g. `abi.encodePacked(0x123,0x456)` => `0x123456` => `abi.encodePacked(0x1,0x23456)`, but `abi.encode(0x123,0x456)` => `0x0...1230...456`). Unless there is a compelling reason, `abi.encode` should be preferred. If there is only one argument to `abi.encodePacked()` it can often be cast to `bytes()` or `bytes32()` instead: https://ethereum.stackexchange.com/questions/30912/how-to-compare-strings-in-solidity#answer-82739. If all arguments are strings and or bytes, `bytes.concat()` should be used instead.

pattern.description: quotePool reads totalSupply() (L517) without the _mintFee LP that pair.mint() issues to feeTo when the V2 fee switch is on.
